short: A scam that impersonates a trusted party to lure victims into handing over data or clicking malicious links.
analogy: Like a fisherman using bait that looks like real food. The fish in a hurry bites right away.

short: Malicious software: viruses, trojans, spyware, ransomware, and the like.
analogy: A guest disguised as a repairman who's actually there to steal.

short: Malware that locks or encrypts the victim's files and demands a ransom.
analogy: A thief who padlocks every cupboard in your house and charges you for the keys.

short: Two-Factor Authentication: logging in requires two kinds of proof, e.g. a password + a code from your phone.
analogy: An ATM needs both the card and the PIN. One alone isn't enough.

short: One-Time Password: a single-use code that's valid for a short time.
analogy: An entry ticket that expires the moment it's used.

short: An app that creates and stores strong passwords, encrypted.
analogy: A key safe: you only need to remember the safe's combination.

short: Scrambling data so only someone with the key can read it.
analogy: A letter written in a secret code only you and your friend understand.

short: A digital fingerprint of data. One-way and not designed to be reversed.
analogy: A blender: fruit becomes juice, but juice can't turn back into fruit.

short: Changing data's format so other systems can send or read it, e.g. Base64. Not a security measure.
analogy: Translating text into Morse code. Anyone who knows Morse can read it.

short: A device's unique address on a network or the internet.
analogy: A home address so packages can reach the right place.

short: The system that translates domain names (google.com) into IP addresses.
analogy: A contact list: you look up a name, it gives you the number.

short: A numbered "door" on a device for a specific service, e.g. 443 for HTTPS.
analogy: One building (IP) has many counters (ports), each offering a different service.

short: A filter for network traffic based on set rules.
analogy: A gate guard checking who can come in and go out.

short: An encrypted tunnel between your device and a VPN server.
analogy: A covered tunnel: people on the street can't see what passes through.

short: The version of HTTP whose connection is encrypted with TLS.
analogy: Talking in a closed room instead of shouting in a market.

short: A small piece of data a browser stores so a site remembers you, e.g. that you're logged in.
analogy: A concert wristband: shows you've paid without queueing again.

short: Cross-Site Scripting: injecting a malicious script into a web page so it runs in the victim's browser.
analogy: Pinning a fake flyer on an official notice board. Whoever reads it gets fooled.

short: Slipping SQL commands in through input so the database runs the attacker's commands.
analogy: Filling an order form with "and give me everything in the warehouse", and the clerk obeys.

short: Guessing a password by automatically trying every combination.
analogy: Trying every key on the keyring one by one until the padlock opens.

short: Manipulating people (not systems) into giving access or information.
analogy: A thief who doesn't break the door, but pretends to be from the power company to get let in.

short: Moving a victim's phone number to a scammer's SIM card to intercept SMS and OTPs.
analogy: A scammer pretends to be you at the post office and redirects all your mail to their address.

short: Capture The Flag: a security exercise or competition to find hidden "flags" through challenges.
analogy: A treasure hunt where the clues are security puzzles.
